title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a cloud-managed runtime keeps email and password off when its deployment declares it off
body:
Fixes #34174

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: on a cloud-managed runtime (`OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`) whose deployment declares `emailAndPassword.enabled: false`, an auth settings save (`PUT /api/settings/auth`) that changes `email_password_enabled` to a value that reads on answers `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` and saves nothing in the batch, where it saved; a stored value that reads on is no longer applied there; and there a Google change no longer counts email and password as a way in. Widened: on that runtime, a save that turns `email_password_enabled` off or clears it answers `200` and saves without the sign-in method floor, where the floor refused it `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`; the field error can carry `constraint: { cloudManaged: true, declaredEmailPassword: false }`; a `managedEmailPassword` copy key in all 11 locales.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the auth settings save or the email and password switch; `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gain the cloud-managed case in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 托管云环境的管理员在 设置 → 认证 里重新打开「邮箱/密码登录」后，登录页不再重新画出一张提交必失败的密码表单；自建部署用户无感。
- 属于托管云环境的统一登录工作，替托管环境的最终用户解决「看得见却用不了的登录方式」。
- 出错时托管环境的管理员保存该开关会被拒并看到说明；已存的旧值不生效、服务端记一次错误日志；可直接撤回本改动。
- 无

## What changes

On a cloud-managed runtime (`isCloudManaged()`) whose deployment declared `emailAndPassword.enabled: false`, email and password stays off whatever the `auth` settings hold. Two places, both in `plugin-auth`:

1. **The settings pass (`bindAuthSettings`, `auth-plugin.ts`).** A stored `auth.email_password_enabled` that reads on is not applied there, so `getPublicConfig().emailPassword.enabled` (what `GET /api/v1/auth/config` serves) keeps answering `false`. Said once at `error` with the remedy (clear the setting), the same level this pass uses for the audience settings it does not apply. An `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED` value (`source: 'env'`) is the deployment's own declaration and still applies.
2. **The save door (`sign-in-method-floor.ts`).** The write predicate on `email_password_enabled` (the sign-in floor's; the settings service keeps one predicate per key) refuses a save of a value that reads on there: `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `invalid_value` at the key, a new localized sentence `managedEmailPassword` in all eleven settings locales, constraint `{ cloudManaged: true, declaredEmailPassword: false }`. Any other save of the key there (off, or a clear) passes, and is no longer judged by the floor: the host holds it off either way, so it removes no way in, and it is how a row stored on is put right. A Google change judged by the floor there reads email and password as off whatever the same save sets it to (contract review S1): a `true` that is no change asks no predicate at its own key, and the runtime would not apply it.
3. **Docs.** `self-hosting.mdx` (the sign-in floor section) and `sso.mdx` (the direct sign-in `off` section) state the cloud-managed case.

**Why both, chosen contract-first.** The card offers "refuse the save" or "do not apply the key". Measured on `main` (below), the save door alone cannot close it: with nothing stored, the key resolves to the manifest default `true`, so the settings service sees a save of `true` as no change, asks no predicate, and stores the row, which the pass then applied. Rows stored before this change are not reached by a save door either. So the guarantee is the settings pass not applying the key on such a runtime, and the save door is the loud refusal wherever the settings service does ask (a change from a stored `false`). Neither half adds a tolerant fallback in a consumer: the deployment's declaration is the authority, and the store is refused, not reinterpreted.

**Admin update-user (the card's last section).** better-auth 1.7.12's `POST /admin/update-user` refuses `data.password` on every deployment (`dist/plugins/admin/routes.mjs`, `PASSWORD_CANNOT_BE_UPDATED_VIA_UPDATE_USER`, 400) before any write. No fix needed; a pin in `cloud-managed.test.ts` holds it on a managed runtime (400 with that code, the member's hash unchanged, the identity-provider user still without a credential), so a vendor upgrade that starts accepting the key reds here.

Self-hosted deployments, and managed ones that declared email and password on, are unchanged (two CONTROL cases).

**Read first (by risk):**

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, the `email_password_enabled` branch of `bindAuthSettings`: the skip condition (`enabled && source !== 'env' && emailPasswordHeldOffByHost(...)`) and the once-only `error`.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, the new first branch of `signInMethodFloorPredicate`: it returns before the floor for every save of that key on such a runtime.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`, the new last `describe`.

## Tests

- New `describe` in `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` (real `AuthPlugin`, real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest, real settings `PUT` route), eight cases: a stored value that reads on is not applied and is said once; a row stored before boot is not applied; turning it on is refused at the save door (envelope `400` + `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, field `invalid_value`, the zh-CN sentence, nothing in the batch written); clearing a row stored on passes; the env declaration still applies; `{ email_password_enabled: true, google_enabled: false }` with Google the last way in is refused at `google_enabled`; CONTROL self-hosted; CONTROL managed with email and password declared on.
- New case in `cloud-managed.test.ts`: admin update-user with `data.password` on a managed runtime.

<details><summary>Premise, measured on main 4af32b99 before any edit</summary>

A probe test (deleted afterwards) booted `AuthPlugin` with `emailAndPassword: { enabled: false }` under `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1` over a real `SettingsService`:

```text
BEFORE false {"value":true,"source":"default",...}
SAVE-TRUE err undefined {"value":true,"source":"global",...}
AFTER-TRUE true
SAVE-FALSE err SETTINGS_VALIDATION
AFTER-FALSE true
```

So `getPublicConfig().emailPassword.enabled` went `false` → `true` on a save of `true`, which no predicate was asked about, and turning it back off was then refused by the sign-in floor.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (each leg through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored to HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

- Settings pass skip removed (`if (!emailPasswordHeldOff)` → `if (true)`): 2 failed / 5 passed of the new describe (the two "not applied" cases).
- Save-door branch removed (`if (key === 'email_password_enabled' && emailPasswordHeldOffByHost(deps))` → `if (false)`): 2 failed / 5 passed (the refusal case, and the clear case, which the floor then refuses).
- S1 condition removed (`localOffered && !emailPasswordHeldOffByHost(deps)` → `localOffered && true`): 1 failed / 7 passed (the Google case).
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- With nothing stored, the settings page reads `auth.email_password_enabled` as the manifest default (`true`, `source: default`) on any deployment that declared email and password off, self-hosted included, while the runtime runs it off. On a managed runtime a re-save of that default is stored and not applied (said at `error`). It is not changed here.
- The display gap above is filed by the seat as #38029.
